q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

problems: figures in no tool result and not one arithmetic step from them: 42,810

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
The data disagrees with the premise — net ROAS is not meaningfully higher; net ROAS averaged ~0.83x (order-date) for 1–13 Oct and is within its normal range, while net profit fell to an average loss of ₹8,108/day in the same window (order-date). The decline in profit is driven by higher ad spend and higher COGS that outpaced the sales gains.

What the data shows
- ROAS vs normal: Net ROAS ≈ 0.83× (2026-10-01..2026-10-13); this sits inside its ordinary daily range and is not an unusual increase versus September.  
- Profit drop: Net profit averaged a loss of ₹8,108/day in 01–13 Oct (net profit on its normal days ranges −₹42,810 to ₹26,973).  
- Main movers (period averages, 01–13 Oct vs Sep reference):
  - Ad spend (P&L basis) ₹54,529/day (+23%).  
  - Contribution margin ₹46,422/day (+36%).  
  - Net COGS ₹31,334/day (+39%).  
  - Orders +23% and AOV essentially flat (₹2,404).  
  - Advertising volume rose significantly (impressions & clicks +291–319%); CPC/CPM fell (CPC −42%, CPM −38%) but cost per order (CPA) +46% and CAC +30% — so cheaper attention but higher cost per converted order and more spend overall.

Why this produces the observed pattern
- ROAS (contribution margin ÷ ad spend) stayed roughly flat because contribution margin grew alongside ad spend; rates improved (lower CPC/CPM) but the extra spend did not convert proportionally into profitable incremental margin.  
- Net profit fell because ad spend (and higher net COGS) increased faster in rupee terms than the additional contribution margin — the P&L line (ad spend + COGS) rose enough to turn contribution into a larger net loss.

Worth checking: break down the extra ad spend by platform and by top campaigns (Meta vs Google and top 10 campaigns) to see which drove the higher spend with poor incremental profit.
